what: Franco-Nevada owns royalties and streams rather than mines. It pays miners money up front in return for a percentage of what a mine produces or sells for the life of that mine, so it earns from metal production without operating costs.
customers: Metal refiners and markets; its counterparties are the mining companies whose output it has rights to.
money: gold, silver and platinum group metals
iron ore, energy royalties and other commodities
moat: A portfolio of hundreds of royalties bought over decades, including interests in some of the world's best mines, with no exposure to rising mining costs.
risks: Profit depends on gold and other metal prices
It has no control over how its partner mines are run
The loss of production at Cobre Panamá removed a large contributor
A low dividend yield of under 1%
opportunities: Operating margin of 74% and net margin of 61%, because it has almost no costs
Revenue grew about 64% last year on metal prices
No debt at all, with $1.2 billion of cash to buy new royalties
watch: Gold-equivalent ounces earned and whether Cobre Panamá restarts.
